findings.charge: The authorityClaim states a reason for this file's existence that a live file at the exact path it cites already satisfies, and the predecessor block omits that file entirely. v1 sits at the artifactPathWhenAuthored the parent names, already pins the accepted parent at 175723e3, and already carries a harness object byte-identical to parent v3's DR-G04 entry. v3 is v1 with a version bump and two citation blocks, published to a path the parent never names.
evidence: Subject authorityClaim: 'This file exists so the D-086 promised artifactPathWhenAuthored is occupied against the accepted parent.'

The harness object the subject carries — which it cannot alter without failing the equality attack — sets artifactPathWhenAuthored to 'docs/coop/artifacts/harness.DR-G04.core-memory.v1.json'. The promised path is v1's. This file is v3, at a path the parent nowhere names, so it does not occupy the promised path; it ships a self-contradicting pointer.

Measured live v1 (sha 568218d7d8337e89, mode 0444): parent resolves to core-gate-harness-specifications.v3.json; parentSha256 is 175723e3a206de5cb6f1b0dd5bb8068c8caf2bef3f1832d55067281d5360b6d2 — the accepted parent, identical to the subject's; and v1.harness == parent v3 harnesses[DR-G04] is TRUE.

Diffed v1 against v3 directly: no key present on v1 only; v3 adds exactly parentReview and predecessorV2; the only shared keys that differ are artifact, version and authorityClaim. v1.harness == v3.harness is TRUE and the two parentSha256 values are identical strings. The substantive payload is byte-identical.
So at authoring time every element of the stated purpose was already true of v1: at the promised path, pinned to the accepted parent, harness object equal to the accepted parent's entry.

The predecessorV2 block names v2 as 'Predecessor' and correctly identifies v2's defect — v2 pins parentSha256 11a305c6d4befc06f12b, the superseded CGHS v2. But it presents v3 as the remedy while never mentioning v1's existence, digest, path or standing, even though v1 is the file the carried harness object points at and the file that already remedies the stale pin at the named path.

Modification times order the line non-monotonically: v2 at 03:02, parent v3 at 03:08, v1 at 03:13, subject v3 at 07:39. v1 is the newer of {v1, v2} despite the lower number, and postdates the parent it pins — consistent with v1 being the current corrected extraction. A predecessor block whose function is custody of the line records this; this one does not.
findings.whyThisIsNotPedantry: Three files now claim to occupy one promised path — v1 'is occupied', v2 'is occupied at v2', v3 'is occupied against the accepted parent' — and two of them, v1 and v3, are pinned to the accepted parent with identical harness objects. A reader following the parent's artifactPathWhenAuthored lands on v1; a reader following this dispatch lands on v3; nothing in either file says the other exists or which is authoritative. The authorityClaim is the load-bearing honesty statement in this corpus — it is what scopes an artifact's reach — and here it asserts a state of affairs that is false of this file and true of a different one. That is not a redundancy complaint; it is a false claim in the field whose whole job is to be true.
refutationAttempted: Read artifactPathWhenAuthored as naming a version line rather than a literal path, so successors legitimately supersede v1. On that reading the promised path is already occupied by v1 and no successor is needed for the stated purpose; on the literal reading v3 does not occupy it. The authorityClaim is false either way, and on the literal reading the carried field actively points elsewhere.

Suppose v1 pinned an older parent when v3 was authored, making v3 the first correct extraction. Refuted by measurement and by clock: v1 carries parentSha256 175723e3 now, and its mtime of 03:13 precedes the subject's 07:39 by over four hours, so v1 already pinned the accepted parent when v3 was written.

Argue the real motive was that v2's pin was stale and v3 avoids reusing v2's number, which is sound custody practice. Granted, and the non-reuse is correct and worth keeping. But then the authorityClaim should say that, and the artifact would still owe an account of v1, which already carries the correct pin at the named path.

Argue redundancy is outside the dispatch's attack list. The list is not exhaustive and ACCEPT requires zero blockers on the merits. In any case the charge is not redundancy but a false authorityClaim plus a material custody omission in the block that exists to record custody.
findings.whatWouldLandIt: State the actual reason for v3 — that v2 pinned the superseded parent and its version number is not reused — and record v1's standing explicitly: its path, digest 568218d7…, that it already pins 175723e3, that its harness object equals the parent's entry, and which of v1 and v3 a reader should follow. If v1 is authoritative because the parent names it, say so and withdraw v3; if v3 is authoritative, say why the parent's artifactPathWhenAuthored resolves elsewhere and what becomes of v1.

notCharged: The subject carries no head, file08Pin, requiredNowUnchanged, reviewStatus or sealRecommendation of its own. v1 and v2 do not either, the artifact is explicitly a thin extraction, and the live parent carries head 5d5d778 and requiredNowUnchanged 26. Requiring those fields here would impose a shape this family does not use.

The threshold block restates the D-006 numerals 40 / 50 / 60 / 100 MB. These are quoted from D-006 clause 4 plus D-102 and match the parent's d006UnitStanding, which holds byteMeaning UNDECIDED; no conversion to bytes is performed and rssProtocol.unit expressly withholds bound comparison. Not an invented constant.

The rssProtocol names concrete primitives — /proc/T/status VmRSS times 1024, task_info TASK_VM_INFO resident_size, a 10 ms sampling window, steady as median at or after 20 ms. These are measurement mechanics carried verbatim from the accepted parent, not D-006 units or RSS bounds, and the equality attack requires them to be carried unchanged.

verdictStatement: REJECT at 1 blocker and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Every attack on the dispatch list is refuted. The harness object is == exact to live parent v3 harnesses[DR-G04] — same keys, same order, same values, equal again under canonical serialisation. The parent pin is CGHS v3 175723e3 and measures true, the parent-review citation and its ACCEPT 0/0 claim check out with no Codex file on disk, OBL-2 is not closed and the live parent agrees, no D-006 unit or binary-MB constant is invented and bound comparison is expressly withheld, analyze and consented-probe RSS are excluded on three separate surfaces, nothing is QUALIFIED or SATISFIED, required-now is untouched, the subject did not move, and v2 is unmoved at 07544950 with its version number not reused. The file fails on its own authorityClaim. It states it exists so the D-086 promised artifactPathWhenAuthored is occupied against the accepted parent, but the harness object it carries names v1 as that path, and live v1 already pins the accepted parent at 175723e3 with a harness object identical to v3's. Diffed directly, v3 is v1 plus a version bump, a reworded claim, and two citation blocks. Three files now assert they occupy one path, two of them identically pinned, and the predecessor block that exists to record custody names only v2 and never mentions v1.
